statements.status_notes: net-imap 0.4.25 includes the upstream quoted-string byte checks from the 0.4.25 release. net-imap 0.3 has no enable method. net-imap 0.3.10 on the Ruby 3.2 leaves carries the same quoted-string check, adapted from https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/7449e180ad6d4211624b7e25138d0b17a86da0fc, which rejects NULL, CR, and LF in quoted strings used for mailbox names and IDs. The advisory fixed version is 0.5.15, so Scout still matches both gems.

net-imap 0.4.25 includes the upstream trailing-literal check from the 0.4.25 release. net-imap 0.3.10 on the Ruby 3.2 leaves carries the same check, adapted from https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/892da94f5c6034028a3aabf27d5981bd41be249c, which rejects a command that ends in a literal continuation. The advisory fixed version is 0.5.15, so Scout still matches both gems.

net-imap 0.4.25 includes the non-synchronizing literal capability check from https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/7228b22b81a49198172fb111a343fef80236bbf5, which refuses to send a non-synchronizing literal unless the server advertises LITERAL+ or a small enough LITERAL-. net-imap 0.3.10 on the Ruby 3.2 leaves adapts that check by rejecting a non-synchronizing {n+} marker inside RawData unconditionally, because 0.3 send_literal never writes one. The advisory fixed version is 0.5.15, so Scout still matches both gems.
